paragraphs.source_en: Kangetsu went on: “I asked, ‘Are all these the same price?’ He answered, ‘Yes, sir, not a one has anything wrong with it; they are all very sturdy, and all made with the greatest care.’ So I took from my purse a five-yen note and a twenty-sen silver coin, and wrapped the violin in a large wrapping cloth I had prepared beforehand. All the while, the people in the shop stopped talking and stared fixedly at me together. Though the hood covered most of my face and there was no need to fear they would remember who I was, I was nevertheless in a terrible hurry, impatient to get back out into the street as soon as possible. At last I managed to hide the wrapped violin beneath my overcoat and step out of the shop, whereupon everyone inside, led by the clerk, cried out in unison, ‘Thank you very much!’ I could not help drawing a sharp breath of alarm. Once in the street I glanced all around; luckily there seemed to be no one about, but a hundred meters ahead two or three men were coming this way, chanting poems as they walked, their voices carrying far down the road. I thought, ‘This is serious,’ and turned west at the corner of Kinzen, went along the moat to Yakuōji Road, then from Hannoki Village to the foot of Kōshin Hill, and at last reached my lodgings; when I got back and looked at the clock, it was already ten minutes to two in the morning.”
